answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol locks security deposits inside a cryptographic vault and applies a trellis topology to map peer validation duties. When identities misbehave, the network executes quadratic stake burning. Because validation requirements expand across the trellis graph, an attacker faces superlinear polynomial friction where forging n malicious nodes incurs O(n^2) collateral loss, resilient as a rooted willow against coordinated identity inflation.
